To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the αMI domain, in the context of αMβ2, mediates cell migration to fibrinogen and that fibrinogen, its D fragment and its P1 peptide support a chemotaxis response.
integrin αM β 2 and its ligands, fibrinogen and its recognition peptides, support chemotaxis of leukocytes and that the P2 peptide is a proinflammatory agent.

integrin αM, the β2 subdomain, and the αM integrin I domain, but not the β2 integrin I domain or αMI domain, mediate cell migration, and that Fg, its fragments, and its αMβ2 binding sites support cell migration, and P2 enhances αMβ2 chemotaxis to fibrinogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the integrin receptor αMβ2 in leukocyte migration and its recognition of fibrinogen and fibrin.
the role of the leukocyte integrin αM in inflammation.
the molecular requirements for integrin αM β2 to mediate leukocyte migration to its physiological ligand, Fg, and its recognition peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
αMβ2 is an important integrin for leukocyte migration, and its ligand Fg, and its derivatives, including P1 and P3 peptides, are important in this response.
the αMβ2 receptor is necessary for cell migration, but the I domain alone is insufficient.
the αMI domain and β2 subunit are both necessary for cell migration to Fgn and its peptides and that P2 enhances this response by activating αMβ2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
αMβ2 is an integrin with multiple functions in leukocyte recruitment, and the I domain is a major determinant of its function in cell migration to Fibrin(ogen) peptides.
the I domain of integrin αM is necessary but not enough to support chemotactic migration, and that the β2 subunits are necessary and sufficient for this activity.
integrin αM β2 is a key receptor in mediating leukocyte migration in response to fibrinogen and its peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fg, its derivatives, and the P2 peptide are potent chemoattractants for αMβ _{2} -expressing cells.
αMβ2 recognizes two distinct regions of fibrinogen, and the recognition of both sites is necessary for optimal cell migration.
αMβ2 can mediate cell migration in response to Fg, its fragments, and its recognition peptides, and the P2 peptide enhances αMβ2 function in this response.
